headline: CORN HOLDS 52-WEEK HIGH; CROP PROGRESS AT 3 PM
subheadline: December corn at $5.22 waits on today's USDA Crop Progress report while Indiana flooding and Iran-Hormuz tensions set up a complicated week.
lead: December corn is sitting at $5.22, at the top of its 52-week range, and doing nothing dramatic while the market waits on Crop Progress at 3 PM CT today. Indiana took nearly 15 inches of rain last week, which is either a late-season quality story or a harvest delay story depending on which fields got hit. The report decides which conversation starts this week.
the_takeaway: Corn priced for good news; today's Crop Progress report tells you if that holds.
teaser: December corn at $5.22 and a USDA report due at 3 PM. The market is positioning, not moving.

one_number.unit: year-over-year rise in July cattle-on-feed inventories
one_number.context: USDA's Cattle on Feed report printed Friday: feedlot inventories up 2% year-over-year, which runs directly against the record-low placements story that has held the feeder complex all summer. More cattle in the system means packer leverage grows, not shrinks, as the import window opens.

yesterdays_call.summary: Called live cattle down toward $217.92 on Aug 23; cattle settled at $223.05 today, never close to that level.
yesterdays_call.note: Missed. Cattle absorbed the bearish Cattle on Feed report without testing $217.92 -- the packer-leverage story may be real but the board did not confirm it Monday. Watch whether the Douglas reopening this week gives the downside case a second chance.

sections.title: CORN WAITS ON THE REPORT
sections.body:
- December corn at **$5.22** is up a penny and a half, no real conviction either way, with the whole complex holding its breath ahead of Crop Progress at 3 PM CT.
- Indiana's historic flooding, nearly 15 inches in parts of the state last week, introduces a late-season quality and harvest-timing wrinkle that the board hasn't priced yet.
- If Crop Progress shows crop condition slipping on the flooding news, this level becomes a launchpad; if conditions hold, the range tightens further.
sections.catalyst: Indiana historic flooding event, nearly 15 inches last week; USDA Crop Progress due 3 PM CT today.
sections.bottom_line: Corn is coiled at a 52-week high waiting for data to tell it which way to go.
sections.farmer_action: If December holds above $5.22 after the 3 PM report, the pricing window Friday's briefing flagged is still open. Do not wait for combines.

sections.title: CATTLE ABSORB TWO-SIDED NEWS
sections.body:
- Live cattle at **$223.05**, off a fraction, absorbing a Cattle on Feed report that showed feedlot inventories up 2% year-over-year, more supply in the system than the low-placements narrative had priced.
- Ag Secretary Rollins reinforced the beef import push over the weekend, calling additional imports necessary to ease consumer costs, which keeps the 90-day import window story alive heading into the week.
- The screwworm-driven phased reopening at Douglas, AZ is set for today, Aug 24; feeder supply mechanics shift the moment that first truck crosses.
sections.catalyst: USDA Cattle on Feed up 2% YoY; Sec. Rollins backing beef imports; Douglas, AZ port reopening today.
sections.bottom_line: More cattle in feedlots plus imports opening equals packer leverage, not feedlot operator leverage.
sections.farmer_action: Cattle feeders: hold major pricing decisions until import volume mechanics and the Douglas reopening pace are clearer this week.

sections.title: ENERGY: HORMUZ BACK ON WATCH
sections.body:
- WTI at **$85.26**, off less than half a percent, but the overnight session saw it test $85.18 as tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz fell to 13 vessels Saturday, the lowest recent count, with the U.S. threatening the toughest sanctions in history against Iran.
- The Iran-Hormuz cycle, a pattern of escalation and deflation running since late April, is back in an escalation phase; the diesel tightness story covered last week is the input-cost risk that actually lands on fall fieldwork budgets.
- Natural gas at $2.84 firmed 2.3%, partly on Japan power disruptions tightening global LNG demand.
sections.catalyst: Hormuz tanker traffic slump to 13 vessels Saturday; new U.S. sanctions threats against Iran; oil down 2% in early Asian trade.
sections.bottom_line: Watch diesel, not crude; the sanctions cycle reprices fieldwork costs before it reprices the futures strip.

outside_the_pit.title: Tyson and JBS Closing or Selling Multiple Harvest Plants
outside_the_pit.body: Tyson is closing its Joslin, IL harvest plant and a Utah case-ready facility, and plans to sell its Pasco, WA plant. Combined with the Cargill multi-plant lockout ongoing since May 19, packing capacity is tightening from multiple directions, a structural shift producers need in their basis math.

outside_the_pit.title: Indiana No-Till Fields Took 15 Inches of Rain Last Week
outside_the_pit.body: Historic flooding hit Indiana no-till fields, with some areas receiving nearly 15 inches in a single week during late pod-fill. Any Crop Progress condition-rating decline in the eastern Corn Belt today ties directly to this event, and harvest timing risk in Indiana is real.

weekly_thread.question: Does Crop Progress show eastern Corn Belt condition damage from Indiana's flooding, or does the crop hold ratings through late August?
weekly_thread.status_text: The report has not printed yet; it releases at 3 PM CT today. Indiana took nearly 15 inches of rain last week, and the answer arrives this afternoon.

the_more_you_know.title: Packing Capacity Is Tightening From Three Directions at Once
the_more_you_know.body: Cargill's lockout removed roughly 6,000 head of daily capacity in May. Now Tyson is closing Joslin and selling Pasco. That is two of the four largest packers reducing throughput in the same season. When capacity falls faster than cattle numbers, basis at the feedlot level widens and packer margins recover at the producer's expense.

watch_list.desc: USDA Crop Progress: corn good-to-excellent below last week's reading flags Indiana flooding damage and adds weather premium to December corn above $5.22.
Douglas, AZ port reopening for Mexican feeder cattle; watch feeder futures reaction, a break below $330 would say the market is pricing returning supply faster than expected.
Weekly export sales: soybeans above 400K MT confirms Chinese demand leg is still active; below 250K MT and the board is on its own.
Iran sanctions details from 'Bessent's Economic D-Day'; any confirmed Hormuz closure or tanker seizure reprices crude and diesel in the same session.

daily_quote.text: Plans are worthless, but planning is everything.
